notes.title: Developer DIary #3
notes.notes:
[p]August has been the month of combat development for the game. For those of you familiar with my other game series, WarPlan, this will have similar mechanics with different formulas and values.

LAND COMBAT
  Multi-hex attacks
  Air may come in as ground support
  99% of the coastline can be invaded
  Artillery phase
  Anti-Tank bonus when defending
  Retreat bonuses with armor when attacking or defending
  Imaged generals can be attached to an HQ

AIR COMBAT
  Ability to attack different targets
  Fighters can fly as a bomber
  Fighters in counters automatically escort their bombers

NAVAL COMBAT
  Spotting has been simplified
  Ship speed is important for searching
  Primary gunnery (11” barrels and larger) + Long Land Torpedo combat round
  Secondary gunnery (4” to 8” barrels) + Torpedo combat round
  Intercept along the way
  Subs alone in a fleet have bonuses to attack

SUPPLY
  Has been simplified only using an attribute called Readiness (5-100%)
  Readiness is lost each turn when not in supply.
  Port supply is simpler. 1 port size supplies 1 land or air unit size of any type
  Supply convoys over sea allow for true island hopping and choke points, adding strategic planning in the Pacific

I created many new sound effects for the game.
Moving icons for damage representation during combat.

Each nation has icons for the most common units of different technologies. A separate selection of NATO or colored icon will be available for map resources, land, air, and naval units. Players can have different settings for each category. 

Early playtesters are getting quite excited about how the game is turning out. I am hoping to put out a simple land/air demo of the invasion of Poland soon. Many players have asked me if you can play a single country. The answer is yes. You can also PBEM with friends, allowing one person per country or 1 person controlling a group of countries. Players are also allowed to grant access for other players to control their units. For example, if you wanted Italy to control German units in North Africa.

The goal is to go to Beta in September and release Spring or Summer of 2026. 

[/p]

notes.title: Developer DIary #2
notes.notes:
[p]This past month, I have been working on all the unit types, unit names, counter names, and divisional names. What I thought would take a week took a month. To give a scope of the size of the work...[/p][p][/p][p]Total Division Types: 626[/p][p]    Many of these are similar with different varieties based on the nation. For example, France has a lower infantry movement rate than Germany, reflecting various factors.
[/p][p]    Aircraft: Each country has historical aircraft grouped by the most common and similar. Aircraft have different statistics. Players can form air counters with a mix of fighters and bombers.
[/p][p]    Naval: Individual capital ships have been researched for accuracy in representation. Even carriers hold the number of planes they did historically. Cruisers come in groups of 4, destroyers and subs in groups of 8. I decided to include light cruisers in the force pool as well.

[/p][p]Total Game Counter Names: 709
[/p][p]    Examples of counter names you will see on the map are 10th Army, or 20th Corps.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Total Game Division Names: 4110[/p][p][/p][p]    Each land counter can hold 60,000 men. Each country has different-sized divisions. The Western Allies have 18,000 men in a division, Germany 15,000 men, and the Soviets 10,000 men. Every strength point a unit has = 100 men.[/p][p][/p][p]    Each air counter can hold 4 air units or roughly 400 planes. Each strength point of an air unit roughly represents 1 operational combat airplane.[/p][p][/p][p]    Each naval counter can hold 6 naval units.[/p][p][/p][p]This entire process has been an enormous task of data entry. It is 96% done. I now have to finish minor countries. Volunteers will double-check my work for accuracy. I want ships and planes to be as close as possible to their realistic attributes while keeping it simple for playability.[/p][p][/p][p]Next is creating the 1939 main scenario. This is another giant beast to tackle. It is the correct placement of hundreds of units on the map from various resources.[/p][p][/p][p]Once this is complete, work will move to coding the remainder of the game.[/p]

notes.title: Developer Diary #1
notes.notes:
[p]To answer your first question, yes I developed the WarPlan games. [/p][p][/p][p]Total Victory is a new brand of my wargames based on the Kingdom, Dungeon, and Hero engine. It has a little more complexity than my WarPlan series keeping with a solid UI and deep strategy.

Due to Kingdom, Dungeon, and Hero's success I decided to transform that engine into World War 2 grand strategy. All of the code had to be adjusted. [/p][p][/p][p]One of the lessons I learned making this game engine is why most games have 1 hex, 1 unit, 1 attack. The difficulty level of creating multi hex attack system with stacks of units is quite challenging. So much can go wrong through user actions or systems interacting. You have to account for every mistake and action a player makes including how fast they play. But this is a game I am excited to make.[/p][p][/p][p]I started with all new art, sound, and music. Total Victory has greater visual detail than my previous series. I also decided to use a realistic map. The editor has been improved as well. Modders will be able to overlay a map onto scenario they create while using the tile system. The map overlay is not required.[/p][p][/p][p]Currently the game's map and most of its menu functions are working. Units can move around. [/p][p][/p][p]I am currently working on inputting all the corps/army names, division names, individual unit classes, and setting up each major power. This needs to be done so I can create the combat system. Land combat is 80% complete. Naval combat is 50% complete.

Some features.

The map uses different scales depending where you are on the map. The Pacific is 4x as large as Europe. So it has a higher movement cost as does the Americas.

1 land, 1 air, and 1 naval counter can stack in a hex.
  Each land counter can hold up to 60,000 men or 6 divisions/brigades/regiments.
  Each air counter can hold 4 air groups.
  Each naval group can hold 6 units with a limit on carriers based on technology.

A land unit strength = 100 men
An air unit strength = 1 aircraft
A naval unit represents the following scale.
  Capital ships: BB, BC, CV, CVL = 1 of that unit.
  CA represent 2 to 4 of that unit.
  DD represent 4 to 8 of that unit.
  SS groups represent 8 of that unit.

Oil impacts the abilities of units.
Manpower impacts the experience of units.

Neither can totally run out. But low amounts impact the ability of units in combat.

This gives a rough vision of the game scale and possibilities.

[/p]
